# TC 4-02.1 First Aid (Excerpt)

## Tactical Combat Casualty Care

### MARCH Assessment Sequence

Perform casualty care during tactical field care using the MARCH sequence.
Address Massive hemorrhage first because uncontrolled extremity bleeding causes rapid death.
Establish an Airway second by clearing obstructions and positioning the casualty safely.
Assess Respiration third by checking chest rise and sealing open chest wounds.
Evaluate Circulation fourth by treating shock and monitoring radial pulses.
Prevent Hypothermia fifth by insulating the casualty from cold ground surfaces.

### Extremity Tourniquet Application

Place the tourniquet high and tight on the injured limb over clothing when the bleeding site is unclear.
Place the tourniquet two to three inches above the wound when the bleeding site is visible.
Do not place a tourniquet directly over a joint such as an elbow or knee.
Tighten the windlass until bright red bleeding stops and distal pulse disappears.
Mark the application time directly on the tourniquet band or casualty forehead.

## Airway Management

Roll an unconscious breathing casualty into the recovery position to keep the airway open.
Insert a nasopharyngeal airway when facial trauma does not prevent nasal passage entry.
